title: IEC 81001-5-1 security risk record
description: One security risk: the threat, the asset and weakness it acts on, and the requirements that control it. This schema is an extension of docs/iso14971/schemas/risk-record.schema.json rather than a replacement for it, and that is the substantive design decision. A security failure that can lead to harm is a hazard; IEC 81001-5-1 adds the analysis that finds it - threat modelling, attack surface, supply-chain exposure - not a second risk file to record it in. Every member the risk record defines keeps its name and meaning here, so a security record can be read by anything that reads risk records, and a security hazard cannot escape the review every safety hazard gets. id, description and controlled_by are therefore still field-aligned with mdux::governance::Hazard, and tools/docs-lint/check_schema_type_drift.py checks that alignment here as well.

id.description: Field-aligned with mdux::governance::Hazard::id. A security record uses the same id space as a safety record on purpose - one risk management file.

controlled_by.description: Field-aligned with mdux::governance::Hazard::controlledBy. Non-empty, every entry naming a requirement - the same machine-checked join as a safety hazard. A security requirement is a requirement: same record, same verification obligation.

hazardous_situation.description: The circumstance in which the threat reaches the asset.

harm.description: The injury or damage that follows. Required, and required to be about harm rather than about the compromise: a security record whose consequence stops at 'data disclosed' has not yet been connected to the risk file this record belongs in.

owner.description: Who this record belongs to. 'device_manufacturer' is the normal case: threat modelling needs an intended use, a deployment environment, a network position and an adversary, none of which a library has. 'mdux' is for the few controls this library enforces regardless of the integrating device.

threat.description: Who or what acts, and how. The security-specific half of the analysis - the part IEC 81001-5-1 adds to ISO 14971 rather than the part it shares.

asset.description: What is being protected - the data, function or property whose compromise leads to the harm above.

weakness.description: The property that makes the threat viable. Free text, but a CWE identifier or similar is preferable where one applies.

attack_surface.description: Where the threat acts from. The closed set names the four surfaces this project can reason about; anything else is device-specific and belongs in the manufacturer's own model.

control_option.description: Which ISO 14971 §7.1 risk control option this record's controls use. Shared with the risk record, and for the same reason: the standard fixes these three and their priority order.

severity.description: A level from the manufacturer's own severity scale. Free text, not an enum - the same reasoning as the risk record: §4.4 of ISO 14971 makes acceptability criteria the manufacturer's to define, and a security record is evaluated against the same criteria.

probability.description: A level from the manufacturer's own scale. For a security risk this is normally an exploitability judgement rather than a failure rate; the scale still belongs to the manufacturer.

acceptability.description: The manufacturer's judgement against its own criteria, after the controls in controlled_by are applied.

scale_ref.description: Where the scales used by this record are defined. Required whenever severity, probability or acceptability is present.

examples.description: A generated artifact shipped with MduX does not correspond to the source and recipe it is recorded as deriving from.
examples.hazardous_situation: A device ships a baked artifact that was edited by hand or produced by an unrecorded toolchain, and behaves differently from the reviewed source.
examples.harm: A clinical display renders from an artifact nobody reviewed, and a user acts on what it shows.
examples.threat: An attacker, or an unwitting maintainer, modifies a committed generated artifact without changing its recipe.
examples.asset: The correspondence between reviewed source and shipped artifact.
examples.residual_risk_note: Covers the build, not a deployed system: an artifact altered after release is outside what this control can see.
